references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus tells the same parable about the unclean spirit that returns and finds the house swept and adorned, and then brings seven other spirits worse than itself.

Peter warns that those who have escaped the world's impurity by knowing the Lord but are again caught will end up worse off than at first—the same principle as in the parable of the swept and adorned house that becomes worse than before.
The Epistle to the Hebrews speaks of those who were once enlightened, shared in the Holy Spirit, yet fell away—a parallel to the house that was cleansed but stood empty and vulnerable to evil.
Jesus warns the healed man not to sin again, lest something worse befall him—a similar principle that a cleansed state requires vigilance to avoid a worse situation.
